items.title: 52043_Herman Autrey oral history interview
items.q: the owner of the theater in Washington, Mr. Litchman, offered me one of the best offers I think I've ever had.

ctx.x: But Herman, was the pay in Philadelphia that much better than the pay in Washington? Or did you want to get out of Washington?

Well, yes. At that time it was better, but I found out later I moved too soon, because the owner of the theater in Washington, Mr. Litchman, offered me one of the best offers I think I've ever had. He wanted me to get my own group. He said I'll put your name in lights. I'll make you -- do this for you. And -- you know, when you're young, and I thought about all the heartaches and things you have going -- trying to have a band, and finding a good musician, which at that time it was too hard to find, I mean to get…
But all this time, at the point that you went to Philadelphia, you never had worked in any of the traveling bands at all, the -- you know, the name bands.
